findings.evidence: Choose the design with fewer entangled decisions, not merely fewer keystrokes.
findings.fix: The model already distinguishes simple from familiar. Keep the two decision questions and the counter-case that a smaller line count can hide coupling; move the restated distinction into the External References note and record the move.

findings.evidence: NEVER drop schema columns, migrations or stored data as entropy reduction
findings.fix: Add the non-obvious recovery case beside that NEVER: a column dropped in an already-applied migration is not restored by reverting the migration file, so the rollback plan must be a forward migration or a restore from backup.

findings.evidence: Use only when the user explicitly asks to reduce entropy, delete code, shrink or simplify a codebase or module
findings.fix: Deletion-biased codebase minimization: inventory code to delete or merge, guard behavior, public APIs and data-retention obligations, and measure first-party line counts before and after. Use only when the user explicitly asks to reduce entropy, delete code, shrink or simplify a codebase or module, rip out what is not needed, or pick the smallest (least-code) implementation, including a request buried in a larger review. Not for general refactoring, readability or local cleanups, performance reviews, or the smallest diff that fixes a bug.

findings.evidence: references/adding-reference-mindsets.md - file template and exclusion list for a new lens; read it when adding a reference, it is not loaded at runtime.
findings.fix: The runtime procedure never points at this optional file. Add one line to step 3b: when the user asks to add a lens, read references/adding-reference-mindsets.md and do not load the decision lenses for that request.

findings.evidence: git ls-files -z ... | xargs -0 -r sh -c 'for f; do [ ! -e "$f" ] || cat -- "$f"; done' sh | wc -l
findings.fix: The measurement is fragile, but the command is not portable: busybox xargs rejects -r, so the counter exits before printing a count. State the default as the same command without -r, and say that an empty list then makes wc print 0; keep -r only as the GNU form.

Give that case an input fixture under evals/files/, such as legacy.py with the polymorphic identity and the Celery decorator, and list it in files so the assertions check the skill against the artifact rather than against the prompt.

findings.evidence: NUL-safe, counts untracked files, skips deleted paths, still reports unreadable ones
findings.fix: The command does not report unreadable files: a permission error on cat prints a diagnostic and the pipeline still exits 0, so the count looks verified. Add '|| printf "UNREADABLE %s\n" "$f" >&2' inside the loop and fail the command when any file is unreadable, matching the rule stated on this line.
A candidate can match two triggers, and the instruction then contradicts itself. Say to load every reference whose trigger matches that candidate and no reference whose trigger does not.
